subject: Urgent: Sedgebrook private cluster throughput regression — exec support requested
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@sedgebrookhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@sedgebrookhealth.com
Date: 2028-07-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden throughput regression on our on-prem cluster — please advise

Vivek / Laura,

We just hit a sharp regression on our Sedgebrook on-prem inference cluster that started around 08:50 PT. Token throughput is down ~60% and P95 latency has moved from ~120ms to ~600ms for our primary billing route. This is impacting customer confirmations and downstream billing jobs.

Attached: prod-telemetry-0729.csv, svc-logs.tgz

Quick notes from our SRE team:
- CPU on head nodes is stable; GPU utilization dropped ~35% around the window
- KV cache hit-rate shows a drop coincident with higher cache misses
- A handful of long-running KVCACHE eviction spikes recorded

We need an urgent action plan and any immediate mitigations you can push on your side. Our CTO Marcus Boyle is on standby. Can you confirm whether any recent config changes, rollout, or model swap happened on Redwood's private control plane for Sedgebrook?

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Ops
Sedgebrook Health

--
Attachments: prod-telemetry-0729.csv (text/csv), svc-logs.tgz (archive)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@sedgebrookhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-29T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput regression on our on-prem cluster — please advise

Aisha — thanks for the alert and the telemetry. I'm pulling the team in now. Short answers up front:
- No deliberate model swap or global rollout was performed against Sedgebrook's private control plane in the last 24h from Redwood's side.
- We are seeing an increased decode cost and KV cache miss in the telemetry you attached.

Immediate next steps I can initiate now from Redwood:
1) Gate traffic to a lower-memory model variant to reduce KV pressure (non-disruptive routing change).
2) Push a targeted KV cache warm/restart sequence on the cluster (short impact, we'll coordinate timing).
3) Open an exec brief and schedule a 30-min huddle with SRE + CTO level if the fixes don't show improvement in 30m.

Can you confirm whether you can tolerate a 10s rolling restart on inference workers? That will transiently affect <2% of in-flight requests if we do it shard-by-shard. If not, we'll prioritize routing to the lower-memory variant first.

Looping in Laura and Marcus from our ops team to validate the warm/restart play and to prepare the runbook.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0119

--
P.S. Marcus, Laura — tagging for immediate triage.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-29T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput regression on our on-prem cluster — please advise

Quick triage notes from ops (internal):
- I pulled the logs Aisha attached. We're seeing a sharp increase in KV cache evictions that align with a GC/eviction loop in the local cache agent. Suspect metadata churn triggered by a rare object version spike.
- Short-term mitigation options:
  * Route Sedgebrook traffic to a compatible, lower-memory quantized variant (reduces KV pressure by ~40% in our benchmarks).
  * Execute a staged KV cache flush + warm sequence using rb-kv-cache-reset.pdf (attached) — expected transient token increase but reduces tail latency.
  * Throttle batch sizes for high-concurrency routes to reduce burst amplification.

I recommend ordering: route -> reduce batch size -> run cache-warm sequence. I'll prepare commands and will coordinate a rolling worker restart if needed.

Attaching runbook: rb-kv-cache-reset.pdf

Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: rb-kv-cache-reset.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@sedgebrookhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Boyle <mboyle@sedgebrookhealth.com>, contracts@sedgebrookhealth.com
Date: 2028-07-29T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput regression on our on-prem cluster — please advise

Vivek / Laura — thanks. We cannot accept a rolling restart during the 09:00-11:30 PT window; that will disrupt batch settlements. Please prioritize non-restart options first (routing or throttling).

Also escalating: our CTO Marcus Boyle will hop on a call in ~15 minutes if this does not stabilize. We are seeing 3.8x increased cost on the critical route and some downstream job failures. PagerDuty incident: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-48321

If routing to a lower-memory variant is a one-click change on Redwood's control plane, please do it now and confirm. We need status in 15 minutes or we will need an exec sync.

Aisha

--
Note: Sedgebrook is flagged as enterprise; contractual SLA impact if not resolved quickly.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-29T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: Sedgebrook private cluster throughput regression — exec support requested

Team — update for leadership and next actions to coordinate with Sedgebrook execs:

Summary (what happened):
- On-prem inference cluster experienced sudden KV cache eviction storm causing p95 jumps and throughput collapse for Sedgebrook's primary route. Initial telemetry attached by customer shows clear correlation.

Actions taken so far:
- Routed traffic to quantized lower-memory variant (completed 09:42 PT). Early telemetry shows throughput improvement ~30% but p95 still elevated.
- Reduced batch sizes for high-concurrency routes (09:50 PT). Observed partial improvement in tail latency.
- Preparing to run staged KV cache warm sequence from rb-kv-cache-reset.pdf; seeking customer approval for short, shard-by-shard execution (estimated 10s impact per shard).

Ask for leadership:
1) Exec participation: Sedgebrook CTO has indicated exec-level call if stabilization isn't seen in 15m. I recommend Vivek + Stephanie + someone from Product (if available) join to authorize temporary SLA concession if customer requests it.
2) Commercial flex: contracts@sedgebrookhealth.com is cc'd; we may need to approve a limited SLA credit if their downstream jobs miss deadlines. Please confirm authority to offer credits up to $10k without legal loop for immediate de-escalation.
3) Engineering priority: Marcus, please prepare the cache-warm command set and a rollback plan. We need a one-page summary we can present on the call (30 minutes).

I'll hold a 10-min prep huddle in 10 minutes in the Ops war room and then escalate to the customer-facing call.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

--
Note: This message included internal notes and next steps for an imminent exec sync.
